Quilombo, directed by Carlos Diegues, was released in 1984 and has since become an iconic Brazilian film. The movie features a powerful performance by João Nogueira, adding depth to its exploration of historical themes.

Monster in the Closet is a unique horror-comedy directed by Bob Dahlin. This American film features notable performances from Fergie and veteran actor John Carradine, blending humor with thrills in a way that has entertained audiences.

Players in the Gallery, directed by Brian Bell, is an Australian film that was released on January 1, 1980. One notable cast member is Peter Sumner, who contributes to the movie's engaging narrative. This film captures a unique aspect of its era while showcasing talent from Down Under.

They Had to See Paris is a 1929 release directed by Frank Borzage. The film features a talented cast that includes Will Rogers, Fifi D'Orsay, and Edgar Kennedy. The screenplay was crafted by Sonya Levien, contributing to the film's charm and narrative depth.

Abundant Acreage Available is a drama film directed by Angus MacLachlan, which was released in the United States in January 2017. Set against the backdrop of rural America, this poignant narrative explores themes of family and loss, making it a compelling watch for fans of the genre.

Bruno Lawrence delivers a captivating performance in the Australian film Pokerface. Set against the backdrop of Australia, this movie showcases his talent and has garnered attention for its unique narrative.

Quilt Treasures is a documentary film that explores the rich history and artistry behind quilt-making in America. This insightful American production delves into how quilts serve not only as functional items but also as significant cultural artifacts, showcasing the stories woven into their creation.

The Farewell is a German drama film directed by Jan Schütte and released on January 1, 2000. The screenplay was crafted by Klaus Pohl, who brought a poignant narrative to the story. 

The cast features notable performances from Ulrich Matthes, Josef Bierbichler, and Birgit Minichmayr, among others. Samuel Finzi and Monica Bleibtreu also contribute to the strong ensemble, enhancing the film's emotional depth.

Now Add Honey, a comedy film directed by Wayne Hope, was released in Australia on January 1, 2015. Set in Melbourne, this lighthearted flick delves into the humorous complications of its characters' lives. The film also received recognition, being nominated for the AACTA Award for Best Actress in a Leading Role, highlighting its strong performances.

sent: Quincy's Quest is a British film directed by Robert Reed, which was released on January 1, 1979. This movie showcases Reed's distinctive style and storytelling abilities, contributing to its unique place in cinema history.

Thieves' Gold is a 1918 film directed by John Ford, showcasing talent from the likes of Molly Malone and Helen Ware. This American production stands out in early cinema history for its captivating performances and storytelling.

Puzzle is a 1977 Australian film directed by Gordon Hessler. Featuring James Franciscus in a prominent role, this intriguing production captivates audiences with its unique story and cinematic style. The collaboration between Hessler and the talented cast showcases the creative landscape of Australian cinema during that era.

Ripkin, directed by Frank Arnold, is an Australian film that was released on January 1, 1978. This notable cinematic work showcases the talent of its director while reflecting the unique artistic vision characteristic of that era in Australian cinema.

Quinneys, directed by Herbert Brenon, is a notable silent film that was released on January 1, 1919. Produced by G.B. Samuelson Productions, this British film offers a glimpse into the cinematic style of its time. Originating from the United Kingdom, it reflects the unique story-telling techniques characteristic of silent cinema.

P.S. Jerusalem is a Canadian documentary film directed by Danae Elon, with a screenplay penned by Sophie Farkas Bolla. This thought-provoking work was released on January 1, 2015, offering a unique perspective on its subject matter. Through its insightful narrative, the film engages viewers with themes that resonate deeply in contemporary discussions.
Raoul Walsh directed the 1918 drama film The Woman and the Law. This early silent film explores themes of justice and morality, reflecting the societal norms of its time.

Rogue Stallion, directed by Henri Safran, is an Australian film released on January 1, 1990. The film features a notable performance by Beth Buchanan, contributing to its engaging narrative and character development. Set against the backdrop of Australia, this production offers a unique perspective that resonates with viewers.

Farewell, directed by Larisa Shepitko and Elem Klimov, is a poignant film based on the novel Farewell to Matyora. Released on October 1, 1986, and later in various international markets, this work features notable performances from Lev Durov, Aleksei Petrenko, and Yury Katin-Yartsev. Produced by Mosfilm, it captures the deep emotional currents of its narrative against a backdrop of cultural upheaval.

Krodham, a rape and revenge film directed by A. Jagannathan, takes place in the vibrant city of Chennai. Released on January 12, 1982, this film features Prem Menon not only as part of the cast but also as the screenwriter, showcasing his multifaceted talent in the industry. The narrative grabs attention for its intense themes and powerful storytelling, characteristic of the genre it represents.

Quinneys, a romance film released on January 1, 1927, is directed by Maurice Elvey. The film features a talented cast, including Cyril McLaglen, Alma Taylor, and John Longden, who all contribute to its charm. Written by Horace Annesley Vachell, this British production was brought to life by the Gaumont-British Picture Corporation.

Geethaanjali, a horror film directed by Priyadarshan, hit theaters in India on November 10, 2013. Featuring the renowned actor Mohanlal, this Indian production combines elements of suspense and the supernatural to deliver a chilling experience for audiences.

Directed by Ulrike Schamoni, Farewell to the Frogs is a documentary film from Germany that offers a unique perspective on environmental issues. This thought-provoking piece was released initially on October 26, 2011, and later saw its publication expanded to March 15, 2012, furthering its reach and impact.

Henry King directed the mystery film The Woman in Room 13, which showcases an engaging blend of suspense and intrigue. This American production features Ralph Bellamy, Gilbert Roland, and Charley Grapewin, all of whom deliver compelling performances that enhance the film's enigmatic atmosphere. The screenplay was penned by Guy Bolton, contributing to the film’s gripping narrative.

Town Bloody Hall is a documentary film directed by D. A. Pennebaker that made its debut in 1979. Originating from the United States, this thought-provoking work explores the feminist movement through a series of engaging discussions and debates.

Enter Nowhere, a horror fiction film directed by Jack Heller, was released on January 1, 2011. This American movie presents a gripping storyline that captures the eerie and unsettling essence of the genre, drawing viewers into its strange and suspenseful world.

The Wonder, a silent biographical film, was released on January 1, 1900. This American production revolves around the life of Ching Ling Foo, showcasing elements of both drama and history. As one of the early examples of cinematic storytelling, the film provides a fascinating glimpse into the life of its subject.

Quinto año nacional is a comedy film from Argentina, directed by Rodolfo Blasco. The film, which premiered on January 1, 1961, features a talented cast that includes Osvaldo Terranova, Alberto Bello, José Maurer, Aldo Bigatti, and Alfonso De Grazia. Abel Santa Cruz penned the screenplay, contributing to the film's comedic elements and narrative depth.
Ulagam is a drama film that was released on July 10, 1953. Notably, the film features a performance by M. V. Rajamma, who plays a significant role in the story.

Abschied von den Wolken, a German thriller film directed by Gottfried Reinhardt, was released on January 1, 1959. The movie features notable performances by Sonja Ziemann and Wolfgang Völz, bringing to life a gripping narrative crafted by screenwriter George Hurdalek.

Carlos Carrera directed a notable drama film that emerged from Mexico in 1995. Featuring performances by Luis Felipe Tovar and Tiaré Scanda, this work explores deep emotional themes in a compelling narrative. Released on October 5, 1995, it has left a lasting impact on the landscape of Mexican cinema.

Directed by Paul Rotha, The World Is Rich is a documentary film that explores themes of wealth and society. Written by Arthur Calder-Marshall, this film was released on January 1, 1947, and showcases perspectives from both the United States and the United Kingdom. Notably, it received a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature Film, underscoring its impact and recognition in the cinematic landscape.

triples.obj: Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature Film

sent: Quisiera Ser Hombre, directed by Abel Salazar, was released on January 1, 1988. This film features Guillermo Capetillo in a prominent role, contributing to its narrative and appeal. The combination of the director's vision and the cast's talent helps to define this notable Brazilian cinematic work from the late 1980s.

Butch Mystique is a documentary film that explores the complexities of identity within the LGBT community. Released in the United States in early 2003, it delves into the experiences of butch individuals, offering viewers a unique perspective on gender and sexuality. This thought-provoking LGBT-related film is significant for its candid examination of themes often overlooked in mainstream media.

High Test Girls, a comedy film directed by Erwin C. Dietrich, was released in Switzerland on January 1, 1980. This Swiss production is notable for its unique blend of humor and storytelling, reflecting the distinctive style of Dietrich's work in the genre.

Parting Glances, directed and written by Bill Sherwood, is a drama film that made a significant impact upon its release on June 4, 1987. This poignant LGBT-related narrative features a talented cast, including Steve Buscemi, Kathy Kinney, Yolande Bavan, and Patrick Tull.

With a modest budget of $100,000, the film successfully captured audiences and later earned Sundance Special Jury Recognition, highlighting its artistic merit. The film explores themes of love and friendship against the backdrop of the 1980s, offering a heartfelt reflection on the challenges faced by the LGBTQ+ community during that era.

Quitting is a captivating docudrama directed and written by Zhang Yang. The film features a noteworthy performance by Jia Hongsheng, who brings depth to the story. Through its unique blend of documentary style and dramatic narrative, this Brazilian film explores complex themes that resonate with viewers.

William V. Mong directed the silent film The Wrath of Cactus Moore, a noteworthy entry in early cinema. This film features performances by Joe Ryan and Lydia Yeamans Titus, both contributing to its engaging storytelling. Silent movies like this one often rely heavily on visual expression, and the cast plays a crucial role in conveying emotions without spoken dialogue.

Directed by Xabi Molia, The Conquerors features a notable performance from Mathieu Demy. This French film explores themes of ambition and confrontation, offering a unique perspective on personal and collective struggles.

Killer's Romance is a yakuza film directed by Phillip Ko that was released in 1990. Set against the backdrop of London, the film intricately weaves elements of the yakuza underworld with the complexities of romance, creating a unique cinematic experience.

The Wrestling Bear is a silent film that was released in the United States in 1899. This early cinematic work showcases the unique charm and simplicity of the silent film era, capturing audiences with its intriguing concept.

Quiz Whizz, directed by Jules White, is a charming comedy film that showcases the talents of cast members Larry Fine, Joe Besser, and Gene Roth. Released on January 1, 1958, this lighthearted feature offers a blend of humor and wit that is characteristic of White's work. The film is a delightful experience for fans of classic comedies, bringing together a talented ensemble to create a memorable viewing experience.

Directed by Alfred L. Werker, The Last Posse is a Western film that premiered on January 1, 1953. This American production features Broderick Crawford in a leading role, contributing to its enduring appeal within the genre. Set against the backdrop of the American West, the film captures the essence of classic Western storytelling.

A Welcome to Britain is a documentary film that was released on January 1, 1943. Directed by both Burgess Meredith and Anthony Asquith, this British film offers a unique perspective on the country during a tumultuous period in history.

Le Péril jeune, a French drama film directed by Cédric Klapisch, showcases the vibrant atmosphere of Paris. The screenplay, penned by both Klapisch and Santiago Amigorena, explores the complexities of youth and relationships. The film features performances from Zinedine Soualem and Élodie Bouchez, both of whom bring depth to their characters. Produced by La Sept, this poignant narrative delves into the lives of its characters amidst the backdrop of the French capital.

Quiéreme porque me muero, directed by Chano Urueta, is a notable Mexican film released on January 1, 1953. The cast features talented actors, including Amparo Arozamena and Abel Salazar, who bring the story to life with their performances. This film stands out in the Mexican cinema landscape of the early 1950s.

The Wrestler, directed by James A. Westman, is a unique blend of action and drama that was released in the United States on January 1, 1974. This film features notable appearances by Ed Asner, Vince McMahon, Ric Flair, and Dusty Rhodes, who contribute to its dynamic storytelling and intense performances.

Death of Merit is a thought-provoking documentary film that delves into the complexities of meritocracy. Through a combination of interviews and in-depth analysis, this documentary challenges viewers to reconsider the societal values surrounding achievement and success.

James Ivory directed The White Countess, a poignant film that was released on January 1, 2006. This American production intricately weaves together themes of hope and redemption against a backdrop of a decaying Shanghai in the 1930s.

Broadway After Midnight is a 1927 silent crime film directed by Fred Windemere. Set in the United States, this intriguing work features notable performances, including one by Matthew Betz. The film exemplifies the unique storytelling capabilities of silent cinema within the crime genre.

Released in 1980, the Indian action film Qurbani, directed by Feroz Khan, features a notable cast that includes Amjad Khan, Zeenat Aman, Bob Christo, and Vinod Khanna. The film is renowned for its thrilling plot and dynamic performances, making it a standout in the action genre of its time.

Freaks of Nature is a unique blend of genres directed by Robbie Pickering, showcasing an ensemble cast that includes Joan Cusack and Vanessa Hudgens. The film's screenplay was crafted by Oren Uziel, blending humor and horror elements to create an engaging story. Shot in Vancouver, this innovative flick also features Patton Oswalt, adding to its quirky charm.

Directed by Doug Sakmann, The XXXorcist is a unique blend of horror and parody that was released on October 27, 2006. This film features Evan Seinfeld and Tommy Pistol, who contribute to its humorous yet chilling narrative. As a distinctive entry in both the parody and horror genres, it both references and satirizes classic horror tropes.

Bhagya Devathai is a compelling drama film directed by Tapi Chanakya. This Indian production explores emotional and societal themes, making it a significant entry in the realm of cinematic storytelling from the region.

Midway Between Life and Death is a gripping horror and thriller film directed by John Real. Set in Italy, this chilling tale features the talented Antonella Salvucci in a lead role, drawing viewers into a suspenseful narrative that blurs the lines between the living and the supernatural. The film expertly combines elements of terror and psychological tension, making it a must-watch for fans of both genres.

Qurbani Rang Layegi is directed by Raj N. Sippy, known for his work in Indian cinema. The film features performances from prominent actresses Padmini Kolhapure and Poonam Dhillon, both of whom play significant roles. Their involvement adds depth to this intriguing narrative that has garnered attention over the years.

Federico Fellini directed the acclaimed comedy and romance film, Variety Lights, which showcases the vibrant atmosphere of Rome. The screenplay was crafted by Ennio Flaiano, adding depth to this enchanting story that intertwines both humor and love in a bustling urban setting.

Astu is a notable film directed by the talented duo Sumitra Bhave and Sunil Sukthankar. Released on January 1, 2015, this Indian production features a compelling performance by Mohan Agashe. The collaboration of these directors delivers a poignant narrative that resonates with audiences, showcasing the rich tapestry of Indian cinema.

Not Me! is a coming-of-age fiction directed by Pierre Gang, showcasing the struggles of youth in a relatable narrative. This Canadian film beautifully captures the essence of growing up and the challenges that come with it.

Mangalya Pallakku, a 1998 Indian film directed by Vinod Roshan, showcases the talents of screenwriter Sathyaraj. This engaging piece features a notable performance by Sreenivasan, contributing to the film's narrative and character development. Set against the backdrop of India, it captures the cultural essence of the time.
Qurbani Jatt Di is an action film directed by Priti Sapru that made its debut in India on January 1, 1990. The film features notable performances from the cast, including the talented Gurdas Maan.

This documentary film, released on January 1, 2016, presents a compelling exploration of its subject matter. Blending factual reporting with engaging storytelling, the work provides an enlightening perspective that invites viewers to reflect on its themes.

Qurbaniyaan, directed by T. L. V. Prasad, features a notable cast that includes Mithun Chakraborty, Mukesh Rishi, and Rami Reddy. This film showcases a blend of talent, bringing together these renowned actors for an engaging storyline. The collaboration of these cast members, under Prasad's direction, contributes to the film's unique appeal.

The Rival of the Empress, an adventure film directed by Jacopo Comin, features a screenplay by Jacques Companéez. Released on February 22, 1951, this Italian production stars Richard Greene in a prominent role, adding to the film's engaging narrative. The film's blend of action and historical intrigue has made it a notable entry in the genre.

Inside Man, directed by Spike Lee, is a gripping heist and drama film set in New York City, released on March 20, 2006. With a compelling storyline that unfolds during a meticulously planned bank robbery, the film features notable performances from James Ransone and Jodie Foster. Produced by Universal Pictures, this movie delves into intricate themes of morality and justice, making it a standout in its genre.

Under Two Flags, a romance film directed by Frank Lloyd, was released by 20th Century Studios in 1936. Adapted from the novel also titled Under Two Flags, this production features a talented cast that includes Simone Simon, John Carradine, and Rosalind Russell. The screenplay was crafted by W. P. Lipscomb, ensuring that the adaptation stayed true to the spirit of the book.

Qué hombre tan simpático is a Mexican comedy film directed by Fernando Soler, which premiered on January 1, 1943. The film features Carlos Orellana in a notable role, contributing to its light-hearted and comedic atmosphere.

Chappie, a South African film directed by Neill Blomkamp, uniquely blends elements of dystopian themes with action-comedy and thriller genres. Set in the vibrant city of Johannesburg, the narrative explores the life of a sentient robot, capturing the challenges and adventures it faces in a society filled with conflict.

With a production budget of around \$49 million, this intriguing film features a screenplay crafted by Terri Tatchell. The cast includes notable appearances, such as journalist Anderson Cooper, contributing to the film's contemporary relevance. Chappie stands out for its engaging commentary on technology and humanity within the backdrop of a richly portrayed South African landscape.

Directed and written by Nurith Aviv, this documentary film debuted in France on January 1, 2011. The work showcases Aviv's unique directorial style, reflecting her commitment to capturing real-life stories and perspectives.

Qué perra vida is a Mexican film directed and written by Jaimec. Released on January 1, 1962, this work features performances from notable actors Gaspar Henaine and Marco Antonio Campos, who contribute significantly to its storytelling.

Under Ten Flags is a drama film that showcases the talents of Italian directors Carlo Lizzani and Duilio Coletti. This film, originating from Italy, is also notable for Coletti's contributions as both director and screenwriter, blending compelling storytelling with rich cinematic artistry.

The Yogi, a 1916 silent drama film, showcases the collaborative efforts of directors Paul Wegener and Rochus Gliese, who also worked on the screenplay. Originating from Germany, this early cinematic work captures the essence of its time through its compelling narrative and visual storytelling.

Step Up 2: The Streets, directed by Jon M. Chu, is a captivating romance film that showcases the vibrant world of dance. Produced by Summit Entertainment, this sequel features Channing Tatum, who brings his charm and skills to the story. The film explores themes of passion and perseverance, set against a backdrop of electrifying dance performances.

Qué tan lejos is a poignant drama film directed by Tania Hermida. Released in Ecuador in 2006, this work delves into the themes of journey and self-discovery, exploring the intertwining lives of its characters against the backdrop of Ecuadorian culture.

Home Team is a Brazilian family and sport film directed and written by Carlos Andrés Morelli. With a production budget of $800,000, the film features César Troncoso in a prominent role. This engaging story is based on a well-known narrative, which adds an interesting layer to its charm.

Social Class in America is a noteworthy documentary that explores the intricacies of class dynamics within the United States. Released in January 1957, it provides a compelling examination of social structures and their impact on American life during that era.

Directed by Orhan Aksoy, Kareteci Kiz is a crime film that focuses on themes of revenge. Released in 1973, this Turkish movie features notable performances by Bülent Kayabaş and Nubar Terziyan. Produced by Erler Film, it explores the darker aspects of justice and personal vendettas, drawing viewers into its intense narrative. The film's compelling storyline and strong cast make it a significant entry in the genre.

Rocky Mountain Rangers, directed by George Sherman, was released in 1940 and features notable performances by Duncan Renaldo and Raymond Hatton. This film showcases the adventurous spirit of the era, capturing the essence of the Western genre with its engaging storyline and charismatic cast.

Dun Huang is a documentary film that explores the rich history and cultural significance of the Dunhuang Caves in China. Released on January 1, 2010, this production from the People's Republic of China provides viewers with an insightful look into this UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Endless Love, directed by Shana Feste, is a romantic film that premiered in the United States on February 14, 2014. This adaptation of the novel of the same name features a talented cast, including Alex Pettyfer, Bruce Greenwood, and Joely Richardson.

Produced by Universal Pictures, this film tells a passionate love story that captures the essence of youthful romance. The film was released to theaters in various markets, including an initial publication date of February 12 and a later release on March 27, 2014.

New Jersey Drive, directed and written by Nick Gomez, is a notable entry in the hood and crime drama genres, released in January 1995. This engaging film features a talented cast including Roscoe Orman, Christine Baranski, Donald Faison, and Heavy D, each contributing to the film's vibrant portrayal of urban life. Produced by 40 Acres & A Mule Filmworks, the film explores the complexities of youth and crime in an impactful way.

American Cowboy is a notable film that was released in the United States in January 1950. This American production captures the essence of the classic Western genre, offering a glimpse into the cowboy lifestyle of the era.

Sous la griffe, directed by Jean Durand, is a noteworthy French film that features Joë Hamman in a prominent role. This intriguing piece showcases the talents of its director and the captivating performance of its cast member, Hamman. With its origins in France, the film reflects the unique storytelling style often associated with the country's cinematic offerings.

Rocky – The Rebel, directed by Suresh Krissna, features a notable cast that includes Zayed Khan, Isha Sharvani, and Minissha Lamba. Released on January 1, 2006, this film showcases their talents in a compelling narrative.

Wong Jing directs the action-comedy The Spy Dad, which features a talented cast including Edison Chen and Tony Leung Ka-fai. This film combines humor with espionage, showcasing the dynamics of a father balancing his secret life with family responsibilities. Audiences can expect an entertaining experience filled with unexpected twists and engaging performances by its star actors.

Hideo Ōba directed The Bells of Nagasaki, a poignant drama film that addresses the tragic events of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Released in 1950, this film is based on the literary work of the same name and features a screenplay by Kaneto Shindō. 

Set against the backdrop of Nagasaki, it explores the profound impacts of nuclear warfare. The cast includes notable performances by Keiko Tsushima, Yumeji Tsukioka, and Osamu Takizawa, who bring depth to this harrowing narrative.

sent: Directed by Pedro Pinho, The Nothing Factory is a musical film set against the backdrop of Lisbon. Released in 2017, this Portuguese production explores themes of work and creativity in a vibrant and innovative manner. The film's unique narrative style and captivating music make it a noteworthy entry in the realm of contemporary cinema from Portugal.

Under the Autumn Rain, a Tunisian film directed by Ahmed Khchine, was released on January 1, 1970. This drama showcases Khchine's skills not only as a director but also as a screenwriter, a role he shares with Ridha Behi. The collaboration between these two talents contributes to the film's unique narrative structure and emotional depth.

Rocník 21, a 1958 film directed by Václav Gajer, brings together a talented cast that includes Hilmar Thate, Eva Kotthaus, Zdeněk Štěpánek, Gerry Wolff, and Josef Vinklář. The screenplay was crafted by both Ota Hofman and Gajer himself, showcasing a collaboration that adds depth to the storytelling. This production is recognized as a remarkable entry in German cinema, reflecting the artistic landscape of its time.

Directed by Gordon Chan, God of War is a historical film that showcases a gripping tale rooted in the past. Released on January 1, 2017, this Chinese production features notable performances by actors Sammo Hung and Vincent Zhao. Set against the backdrop of the People's Republic of China, the film delves into themes of honor and conflict.

Stille Nacht, directed by Ineke Houtman, is a thrilling film from the Netherlands that was released on September 16, 2004. This gripping thriller features a talented cast, including Victor Löw, Caro Lenssen, Marcel Musters, Lore Dijkman, and Liesbeth Kamerling, all of whom deliver compelling performances. The screenplay was crafted by Frank Ketelaar, contributing to the film's intense narrative and suspenseful atmosphere.

Sous la terreur, released on January 1, 1936, is a notable film directed by both Marcel Cravenne and Giovacchino Forzano. Featuring the talented Marie Bell, this cinematic piece offers a compelling narrative that reflects the artistic styles of its time. The collaboration between the directors and the cast member contributes to its historical significance in cinema.

Roco Kingdom: The Desire of Dragon is a 2013 animated feature directed by Sheng-jun Yu. This Chinese film transports viewers to a fantastical world, showcasing its vibrant animation and engaging storytelling that reflects the creativity emerging from the People's Republic of China.

Stranding, a film directed and written by Louis van Gasteren, first premiered on February 5, 1960. This Dutch production showcases the unique vision of its creator, who captures the essence of the Netherlands in a captivating narrative.

Vallanzasca - Angels of Evil, directed by Michele Placido, is a 2010 crime film that explores the notorious life of the Italian gangster Renato Vallanzasca. The storyline is set against the backdrop of Milan, where much of the film was filmed, immersing viewers in the gritty urban landscape that defined Vallanzasca's criminal activities.

The cast includes notable performers such as Paz Vega, Moritz Bleibtreu, Kim Rossi Stuart, and Michele Placido himself, who also contributed to the screenplay. This film, which showcases a blend of French and Romanian influences, provides a compelling peek into the underbelly of crime in Italy during the 1970s.

Sweet Thieves is a Brazilian comedy film directed by Fernando Coni Campos. Its humorous storyline showcases the unique cultural landscape of Brazil while delivering a blend of laughter and charm. The film highlights the directorial talent of Campos, contributing to the rich tradition of Brazilian cinema.

Under a Texas Moon, released in 1930, is a musical film directed by Michael Curtiz. The screenplay was crafted by Gordon Rigby, adding depth to the storyline which features a talented cast including Myrna Loy, Noah Beery, Sr., and George E. Stone. Alongside these names, Tully Marshall and Charles Sellon also deliver memorable performances in this American production. This film showcases the vibrant energy of early musical cinema, characteristic of its time.

Powerful: Energy for Everyone is a Canadian documentary film directed by David Chernushenko. Released on June 8, 2010, this insightful work explores the vital topic of energy and its impact on our everyday lives. The film delves into various aspects of energy production and sustainability, emphasizing the importance of accessible and renewable energy sources for everyone.

Rocío de La Mancha is a musical film directed by Luis Lucia Mingarro, who also contributed to its screenplay. Set in Spain, this vibrant production features performances by José María Caffarel, Jesús Puente Alzaga, and popular Spanish singer Rocío Dúrcal. With its engaging cast and lively musical numbers, the film showcases the rich cultural tapestry of its country of origin.

Directed by Fernando Coni Campos, Uma Nega Chamada Tereza is a Brazilian comedy film that was released on January 1, 1973. This lighthearted feature offers a mix of humor and cultural insights unique to its time and place, showcasing the talents of its creator and the vibrant backdrop of Brazil during the era.

Gakkō no Kaidan is a Japanese horror film directed by Hideyuki Hirayama. The movie features a talented cast, including Akira Kubo, Takashi Sasano, and Kimiko Yo, who each contribute to the chilling atmosphere. Set in a school, this intriguing film explores ghostly encounters and eerie experiences, captivating audiences with its suspenseful storytelling.

Theodor Hierneis oder Wie man ehem. Hofkoch wird is a German drama film directed by Hans-Jürgen Syberberg. Released on January 1, 1972, this thought-provoking piece features Walter Sedlmayr in a prominent role. The film weaves a narrative that reflects the cultural and historical context of Germany during that era. Its striking direction and compelling performances contribute to its status as a significant work from the early 1970s.

Code Name Melville, directed by Olivier Bohler, was released on January 1, 2008. This French film features an impressive cast that includes notable names such as Volker Schlöndorff, Johnnie To, and Jean-Pierre Melville, each contributing to its unique narrative and artistic vision.

Rodinné trampoty oficiála Tříšky is a comedy film directed by Josef Mach, with a screenplay crafted by Ivan Osvald. This delightful Czech production features a talented cast, including Karel Effa, Josef Kemr, Felix le Breux, and Rudolf Hrušínský. The film combines humor with relatable themes, making it a memorable addition to the comedy genre.

A Litre of Tears is a poignant Japanese drama film directed by Riki Okamura, released on January 1, 2005. The narrative is based on the true story depicted in 1 Litre no Namida, and it features a powerful performance by Yoshimi Ashikawa. This moving tale explores human resilience and the challenges faced by those dealing with illness.

Rodney Rude Live Volume 1 is an Australian comedy film that was released on January 1, 1984. This film captures the outrageous stand-up performance of the iconic comedian Rodney Rude, showcasing his infamous routines that blend humor with a distinctively provocative style.

Directed by Tetsuo Shinohara, Flower and Sword is a poignant drama film from Japan.
